key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves current collection and overall efficiency in AlInN/Si solar cells without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, semitransparent conductive contact that can boost nitride-based photovoltaic device performance while remaining compatible with wafer-scale integration.
method: Grow AlxIn1-xN (x = 0.22, 0.35, 0.43) on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer.
Transfer a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as the semitransparent contact.
Compare photovoltaic behavior with and without graphene under illumination and dark conditions.
evidence_signal: Across all three compositions, the abstract reports higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency with graphene, while open-circuit voltage stays nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The benefit depends on a successful low-temperature graphene transfer and consistent contact quality, which may be challenging to reproduce at scale.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
